blocks.packageReason: Tier C, PACKAGE with a written reason: the library's effect.remove-item takes only a 'who' and removes an unspecified item; this rule removes ONLY berries, ALL stacked copies, from EVERY adjacent foe, refreshes the modifier bar and shows a message per foe. There is no item-kind filter, no 'every stack' mode and no 'all adjacent foes' scope in the library, so the effect would have to be re-implemented; request R20 asks for effect.remove-item to grow those three options (kind: berries, all copies, who: adjacent foes). The trigger (on entry) is a separate block and extra IFs can be ANDed on top. Users: Power of Alchemy (223, attr 0) only. blocks.packageReason: PACKAGE, written reason: the survive rule (clauses 1 to 4) is inherited from PreFaintReviveAbAttr (B11), whose canApply is not mine to split, and the effect (a STURDY tag that the damage pipeline reads, plus a per-switch-in marker that the matching end-of-turn attr reads) has no library effect: there is no 'survive a lethal hit' block and no 'set a marker' block. Requests R1 (split the inherited canApply into a swappable 'the hit would knock me out' condition) and R2 (effect: survive a knockout at 1 HP) in requests/B17.md. Typed params: none exist; the only number in the chain is the inherited HP rule threshold 0, which is always true. Users: Lingering Musk (6084, attr 2) only; its attr 3 is LingeringMuskPostTurnAbAttr. SUSPECTED GAME BUG, NOT FIXED: this class's apply sets tempSummonData.lingeringMuskFaint = true without checking `simulated`. PreDefendFullHpEndureAbAttr is dispatched from Pokemon.getAttackDamage with the caller's `simulated` flag, and getAttackDamage(simulated: true) is called for damage previews (move-phase.ts:682 and move-effect-phase.ts:1071 target ordering, the enemy move scoring in pokemon.ts around lines 10040 to 10360). A previewed knockout of a Lingering Musk holder (damage >= hp) therefore sets the marker although no hit landed, and the holder faints at the end of the turn. Needs a check by the owner; the declaration records simulated: ignores.

blocks.label: Make the Pokemon that knocked me out faint too
blocks.summary: When I faint from an attack, the Pokemon that knocked me out loses all of its remaining HP, as long as it is still standing and not on my side.

blocks.packageReason: Tier B with a PACKAGE effect. Written reason: the effect is one damageAndUpdate(attacker.hp, INDIRECT) call, but no library effect 'knock out another Pokemon / take all of its remaining HP' exists (request R7 in requests/B17.md); recoil and drain scale with a damage or max-HP share and apply to the holder or the damage dealt, not 'all current HP of the other Pokemon'. The trigger (when I faint) and the one real condition (the knocker is not an ally) are separate blocks. The three guards (a move, a known attacker, still standing) have no registry ids (request R8), so they are written as feasibility; they run first, in the original order, before the gate. The condition used to be `!attacker.getAllies().includes(pokemon)`: getAllies() lists the OTHER ACTIVE battlers on the attacker's side, the atom side.is(ally) compares isPlayer() and identity. They differ only if the knocker is on my side but I am no longer in the field array (not reachable: the faint dispatch runs while I am still on the field). The L1 grid never sets a same-side attacker, so test/tests/elite-redux/decomp/B17/gates.test.ts checks both directions with stand-ins (the old canApply, the refactor, the rebuild and a deliberately wrong gate), and mutual-destruction.test.ts runs the foe direction in a real battle. A real double battle for the ally direction is not possible here: the existing innards-out.test.ts double case also times out in this checkout. Users: Mutual Destruction (6104, attr 0) only. The ability also carries the ability-level flag bypassFaint (set in wireBernerdRosterAbility, not an attr), which belongs to the ability blueprint, not to this block. The ability text mentions Pain Split first; the code deals the attacker's whole current HP directly (the comment in apply says that equals the Pain Split plus Innards Out result), so no Pain Split step exists in this attr. No game bug found.

Written reason: the effect writes two string markers in the ER provenance memory (battleData 'oracle:first-entry', summonData 'oracle:guard:N'), and a closure of ANOTHER attr (ReceivedMoveDamageMultiplierAbAttr in Oracle, bound legacy in the precedents) reads them back by string prefix; there is no library effect to set a typed marker (request R9) and no atom to read it (request R3). The number of turns is the typed `guardTurns` setting (1 to 10; the class itself accepts any number, 0 or less would start an already-expired guard). The gate binding is legacy-closure-pending-request R3, so the rebuild is skipped by L2. Users: Oracle (6047, attr 1) only. Oddity, not changed: the ability text says incoming attacks are 'treated as not very effective', but the damage attr halves the damage (x0.5), which is what the guard does in code. Replacing an existing guard marker means a second entry in the same battle never restarts the guard (the first-entry memory blocks it).

The package still has a typed number (power 1-250) and the trigger and condition are separate, swappable blocks. The gate is legacy-closure-pending-request R10 (move.is-move cannot name Five-Star Fury because it only exists in ErMoveId); until R10 exists the attr cannot be rebuilt from the library. Users: Penta-Punch (6015, attr 1) only; attrs 0 (marker), 2 (priority +1 for Five-Star Fury, a closure) and 3 (+1 crit stage for Five-Star Fury) belong to other classes and use the same move test, so R10 serves them too. Oddity, not a bug: apply overwrites the power instead of multiplying, so any power multiplier applied earlier in the chain is thrown away and later ones still apply; this is what the ability text asks for. feasibility: My attack must have landed earlier this turn: the matching 'mark that my attack landed' block leaves a marker that this block uses up
A foe must still be standing, otherwise nothing is queued (the marker is used up anyway)
It never queues anything for a preview (a simulated end of turn)
blocks.packageReason: Tier B with a PACKAGE effect. Written reason it cannot be split further: the effect is one ordered, stateful sequence (use up the marker, find the first living foe, reset the streak if a chain was already pending, mark the chain pending, queue a Rollout that carries the marker 'perpetual-motion' and has its consecutive-use power stripped). The library's effect.scripted-move cannot reproduce it: it has no marker option, no 'strip consecutive-use power' option, it needs the foe that was hit (here there is none: the first living foe is picked) and it writes none of the chain state that the Progress, Power and Resolution attrs read (request R14). Typed param: power (the Rollout's power, 1-250). The Rollout itself and the marker names are fixed. The marker check (clause 3) stays as `residual` because it is the coupling between the two halves, not a design choice, and `apply` tests it again; requests R3/R15 name the library atom and effect for the marker memory. Users: Perpetual Motion (6022, attr 1) only. The turn-count gate has the exact atom `time.turn-count` (>= 1 turn, same field tempSummonData.turnCount). Oddity, not a bug: apply removes the marker BEFORE it looks for a foe, so when no foe is standing the marker is lost with no Rollout. No game bug found.

blocks.packageReason: Tier B with a PACKAGE effect. Written reason: the effect writes two fields of per-switch-in chain state (erPerpetualMotionPending and erPerpetualMotionStreak) that the Progress and Power attrs of the same ability (B14) also read and write; there is no library effect or atom for a named chain flag and counter (request R16), and splitting it would invent behaviour. No typed param exists: nothing numeric is used. The gate (my last move was Rollout) is the exact library atom time.last-move, but its binding is legacy-closure-pending-request R22: the shared L1 proves gates through canApply, this class runs its gate inside apply, and the my-move-starts trigger has no engine-parameter builder in the harness (the equivalence is proved by hand in penta-perpetual.test.ts); the residual (pending, indirect, not a success) stays in the class as feasibility, with request R17 for the atoms that would let it be promoted into the gate. Users: Perpetual Motion (6022, attr 2) only. The gate runs inside `apply`, not `canApply` (the inherited canApply is `true`), so the ability flyout is queued at every one of my moves even when nothing happens; this is existing behaviour, kept. No game bug found.
